name: Afrocentrism
summary: Afrocentrism, called Afrocentricity by its main theorist Molefi Kete Asante, holds that African peoples and their descendants should be studied and should act as subjects of their own history, not as objects seen through European frameworks. It treats Eurocentric scholarship as a particular outlook passed off as universal and seeks to recover African cultural memory, drawing on Cheikh Anta Diop's case that ancient Egypt was an African civilization. Politically it favours African unity and self-determination, from Diop's federated Black African state to Asante's United States of Africa, and communitarian values such as Maulana Karenga's Nguzo Saba. It says little about conventional economic and social policy.
scope: Academic Afrocentricity (Asante, The Afrocentric Idea, An Afrocentric Manifesto, his 2010 United States of Africa essay), Karenga's Kawaida and Nguzo Saba, Diop's historiography and federal programme in Black Africa, and Marimba Ani's critique of European culture in Yurugu. Excludes the hotep subculture and melanin theories, which critics associate with popular Afrocentrism, except where noted. Most policy statements fall outside the documented scope and are inferred with low confidence.

missingStatements.text: School history curricula should centre the achievements of the students' own ancestral civilizations rather than treating European history as the norm.
missingStatements.rationale: Asante argues students must be placed at the centre of instruction and that Eurocentric content is wrongly imposed as universal.

missingStatements.text: Ancient Egyptian civilization was created by Black Africans, and its heritage belongs to Africa.
missingStatements.rationale: Diop wrote that ancient Egypt was a Black civilization, and Afrocentrists commonly share this thesis, which historians such as Lefkowitz dispute.
missingStatements.declined: A specific empirical claim about ancient history disputed by historians, not a position other ideologies would take sides on.

notes: Highly heterogeneous; academic Afrocentricity differs from popular Afrocentrism and hotep communities. Critics such as Mary Lefkowitz, Stephen Howe and Manning Marable dispute its historical claims and political value (attributed context only). Karenga's early US Organization practised gender complementarity and armed self-defence; later Kawaida softened on both and on religion. Most policy answers are inferred.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a healthcare doctrine; the communal ethos of Umoja and Ujima suggests support for collective provision, but no source states it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the community-economic focus of Kawaida and concern for Black economic standing; no source addresses wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ujamaa favors community-owned cooperative enterprise and Asante says commerce harmed Africa, so unfettered markets are viewed skeptically; not a developed doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Ujamaa stresses community-owned business, which is cooperative rather than clearly state ownership; adherents range from nationalization to Black capitalism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from collective-responsibility ethics; sources are silent on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Collective work (Ujima) and solidarity make support likely, though unions are not a theme in the sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: Communal ownership and cooperative economics (Ujamaa) lean away from treating private property as near-absolute; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Asante holds that international commerce has harmed Africa, implying support for restraining corporations; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Community mutual support and attention to Black disadvantage make cutting welfare unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ujamaa calls for building and sharing in community-owned businesses, close to but not identical with worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Black nationalists such as Karenga's US Organization were targets of COINTELPRO, making state surveillance suspect; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement is not unified on drug policy; no source addresses it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Afrocentrists oppose racism but there is no documented position on legal speech limits; adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: No doctrine of strongman rule; Asante stresses community awakening and agency of people, inferred against.

state-harmful.rationale: Afrocentrism builds institutions and a nation-state ideal (Diop's federal state), so a stateless view is foreign to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Karenga's US Organization practiced armed community self-defense, yet adherents are split on gun law; no stated position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Black nationalist movements experienced policing as hostile (the COINTELPRO feud); inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Critics note hotep strands police women's sexuality, and Kawaida emphasizes family and community values; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Self-determination (Kujichagulia) is community-level, but Diop wanted a continental federal state; mixed.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from criticism of the carceral treatment of Black communities and community-building ethos.

traditional-family.rationale: Karenga's Umoja calls for unity in the family first, and Kawaida places family rituals and the rites of the life cycle at the base of community.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The sources consulted do not state a position; critics link popular and hotep Afrocentrism to anti-gay attitudes, while academic Afrocentrists are divided, so this is inferred and contested.

abortion-legal.rationale: No documented movement position; adherents are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Asante says Afrocentricity can coexist with many faiths while Karenga is a secular humanist; the movement is split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Asante's stated aim is to lift discussion of African people out of Eurocentric victimization and objectification, and his education essay treats the marginalizing of Black students as a wrong that schools must actively undo.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not a stated position; critics associate hotep strands with anti-feminism and essentialist views.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida programme calls culture the basic source of a people's identity, purpose and direction, and Asante builds his theory on recovering African cultural location.

gradual-change.rationale: Karenga calls for a cultural revolution and constant, conscientious struggle, and Asante frames his work as a critique of the established social order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Pan-African ideals of unity and diaspora return suggest welcome of African-descended migrants; no direct statement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Asante argues Africa was betrayed by imported structures and commerce; skeptical of Western-dominated bodies, though pan-African unions are favored.

free-trade.rationale: Asante's Manifesto questions claims that globalization spreads universal liberal-market norms, and Diop wanted Africa's economy organized by a federal state rather than left to world markets.

nation-first.rationale: Own-people interests come first (Kujichagulia, Diop's federated Africa), though the unit is the African people rather than a country.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No documented position; sovereignty concerns versus anti-atrocity concern.

open-borders.rationale: Pan-African unity implies open movement within Africa but no stated view of borders generally.

limit-growth.rationale: Not an environmental ideology; focus on Black economic development makes growth limits unlikely.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Karenga laments a relentlessly degraded environment and calls for repairing the world, but climate policy is not addressed, so this is inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Diop praised African scientific achievement but no doctrine on technological progress as salvation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Diop, a nuclear physicist, listed atomic and thermonuclear energy among the resources a federated Africa should develop; other adherents are silent.

revolution-justified.rationale: Karenga's US held that a cultural revolution must precede a violent revolution, and his programme still speaks of continuing the cultural revolution of the 1960s.

experts-over-public.rationale: Afrocentrists attack Eurocentric academic expertise as biased, so deference to experts is unlikely.

central-planning.rationale: Diop wanted rational economic organization at federal level but no endorsement of planning as such.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ujamaa asks Black communities to build their own stores and businesses and profit from them together, a market economy built on collective ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

basic-income.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Diop sought an economically unified Africa shielded from external dominance; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Diop's programme assigns investment funds and regional industrial engines to a federal state; this reflects Diop's plan more than all Afrocentrists.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cooperative ownership favored but no stand on small property per se.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Cooperative businesses are not abolition of money; no source supports it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No support in the sources; inferred as foreign to the movement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

one-party-rule.rationale: Not stated; Karenga's own organization was a cultural-political body but the ideology lacks a one-party doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Some adherents prize African kingship and Kemet's pharaohs but there is no stated doctrine.

democracy-best.rationale: Diop proposed a bicameral democracy for his federal state and opposed Senghor's regime as undemocratic, but most Afrocentric writing does not rank forms of government.

direct-votes.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

workers-councils.rationale: No evidence of council-based politics; community-based unity instead.

right-to-secede.rationale: US Organization pushed for a separate political structure for African Americans, and self-determination is a core principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Afrocentrism rejects racial hierarchy of rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Karenga's movement practiced armed self-defense and rejected pacifism; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Karenga is a secular humanist and later said Kwanzaa was not meant to replace anyone's religion; strict separation is inferred and spiritual strands differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Karenga rejected Christianity as basis for identity and favors secular humanism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Cooperative, communal ethos goes against privatizing security; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Diop's federal state of Black Africa and Karenga's view of Black people as one people presuppose a shared African identity as the basis of political community.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Asante's Manifesto, as reviewed by Smith, rejects the Marxist paradigm because it centres market production rather than culture; Afrocentricity reads history through cultural agency and race.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Ujamaa's shared wealth points toward equality, but the Nguzo Saba also endorse community-owned businesses that profit; no stated view on outcome equality, so this is inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonialism and self-determination; some adherents extend African identity to indigenous peoples elsewhere.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Diop calls imperialism's destruction of African culture a killing of the people's being, and Afrocentrists seek redress for the Maafa; reparations policy itself is not stated in the sources consulted.

civilizational-union.rationale: Diop campaigned for a federated Black African state and wrote that rational economic organization cannot precede Africa's political unification; Asante argues for citizenship in a United States of Africa.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Karenga explicitly condemns vulgar individualism and predatory appropriation, setting shared work and shared wealth against them.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Nguzo Saba frame obligations to family, community and people, such as collective work and responsibility, as the core of the moral life.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ani's critique of Europe's treatment of matter as dead and Karenga's call for profound respect for the environment point this way; it is inferred rather than stated.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Afrocentric hostility to outside control over African peoples.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Diop wanted regional industrialization of Africa, though Ani's critique of European domination of nature pulls the other way; the answer is inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

human-enhancement.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Asante stresses human agency and subject place; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

restore-past-order.rationale: Afrocentrists look to Kemet and African tradition for values but pair this with modern development, so restoration versus progress is not a stated choice.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents hold a committed worldview centered on African agency.

direct-action.rationale: Karenga's US Organization and the Black nationalist tradition emphasized community organizing and self-defense beyond elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Kawaida builds the desired community culture through cultural practice (Kwanzaa, principles) in the present.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Diop credits Africans with inventing agriculture, sciences and arts; foraging is not an aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Ujamaa is cooperative sharing but is not a stated need principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Cooperative community economics aims at collective benefit rather than private profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Asante claims commerce harmed Africa but there is no Marxist labor theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Asante rejects the Marxist paradigm as centred on production rather than culture, so class dictatorship has no place in Afrocentric politics.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective work is valued but farm collectivization not stated.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Commerce is blamed for harm to Africa, but no theory of inter-imperial war.

harm-principle.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Kujichagulia grants self-determination to peoples as well as persons, and Karenga speaks of the rights of all to a just share of the world's goods, so rights are not only individual; Asante also stresses personal dignity.

conscription.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Unity and community-building stress staying engaged; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Communitarian ethic rejects customer relation to state; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Asante ties freedom to economic as well as political and cultural freedom, and Karenga asserts a right of all to a just share of the world's goods.

media-academia-power.rationale: Afrocentrists see academic and media institutions as carrying Eurocentric assumptions and shaping what counts as knowledge.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Asante states that Afrocentricity is not a Black version of Eurocentrism and does not condone valorizing one group by degrading others, which rules out racial hierarchies of ability; genetics itself is not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

national-rebirth.rationale: Asante's Manifesto is subtitled Toward an African Renaissance and Diop is a symbol of African rebirth after colonial cultural destruction.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Aim is unity and sovereignty of Africa, not conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oath-based authority appears nowhere in the sources; inferred as foreign to a movement built on community unity and self-determination.

bound-labor.rationale: Afrocentrists treat enslavement, the Maafa, as the central historical crime against Africans, so bonded labour is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Outlaw summarizes the paradigm's core insight as all knowledge being centred on particular values and interests, and Asante holds that Eurocentric perspectives are imposed as if they were universal.

universal-morality.rationale: Asante treats claimed universals as Eurocentric particulars, though Karenga's Maat ethics speaks of a common ground of humanity; the answer is inferred and adherents differ.

single-common-good.rationale: Communal common purpose (Nia) but no claim of one rationally derived good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents are split, with no consistent position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Afrocentrists regard all African-descended peoples as Africans, and older Black nationalists promoted return; academic Afrocentrists do not state a citizenship policy, so this is inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Diop called for choosing an African language and raising it into a modern language of culture and the state, holding that African languages would regenerate African culture.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cooperative economics suggests shared control over enterprises.

school-vouchers.rationale: Asante sees curricula as vital; vouchers could aid Afrocentric schools but no position.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

economic-freedom.rationale: Asante links economic to political and cultural freedom, but not in the liberal sense.

rule-by-example.rationale: Imani asks belief in leaders; not a doctrine of rule by example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Kujichagulia, self-determination, is one of Karenga's seven principles, which he defines as every person's and people's right to freedom and flourishing; Diop's work grew from the struggle for African independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Karenga is a secular humanist, but the movement stresses culture and spirit; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Pan-African solidarity against restrictions on migrants; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cooperation within the community across classes, though Marable criticized middle class orientation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Recovering and preserving African cultural memory is the core Afrocentric project; Diop and Karenga treat heritage as the base of creativity, not an obstacle to it.

dominated-front.rationale: Afrocentrists seek African unity against Western cultural hegemony, but Asante says Afrocentricity seeks partnership and neither imposes on nor seeks advantage over others, so a broad anti-Western bloc is a weaker fit than African unity.

workers-nation.rationale: Identity is racial and civilizational rather than class-based.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Early US practised gender complementarity, which Brown lists among its failings as sexism, while later Kawaida and many Afrocentrists reject it; adherents are split.

ban-interest.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Afrocentricity grew out of the Black freedom movement and Asante's multiculturalism is explicitly nonhierarchical; legal segregation is the system adherents historically opposed. Cultural self-organization is distinct from state-imposed separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Afrocentrism frames domination through race and culture rather than class, so it has no stated theory of the state as a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Afrocentricity is a critique of the demand that Africans adopt the dominant European culture; Asante and Karenga urge cultural self-definition instead.

elite-replacement.rationale: No Afrocentric source endorses a replacement conspiracy; inferred from the movement's focus on African agency rather than immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

national-mission.rationale: No such civilizing mission; opposes imposing worldview.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Afrocentric sources do not analyze patriarchy; critics accuse hotep strands of anti-feminism while others adopt gender equality, so adherents are split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: No stated position beyond criticism of white power structures.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Opposed to eugenics, historically used against Black people.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Black nationalists faced state repression (COINTELPRO), supporting accountability; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Communal cooperative ethos goes beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Some strands favor racial solidarity but mainstream scholarly Afrocentricity does not mandate it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Asante defines multiculturalism as nonhierarchical and rejects degrading other groups, and Karenga's Umoja begins from the common ground of humanity.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial framing makes it likely; not specifically addressed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Asante accepts coexistence of many faiths.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Karenga is secular, though Afrocentric theology exists; split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

trade-surplus.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

population-transfer.rationale: Opposed as an instrument of historical oppression of Black people.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not an absolutist ideology; Karenga's movement practiced armed self-defense.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Asante frames Africans as subjects not objects, free of white domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

vanguard-party.rationale: Karenga's organization was a disciplined cultural-political group, but no doctrine on a vanguard.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Asante blames commerce and external structures for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not a position held; adherents center their own cohesion not anti-diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Black nationalists were victims of such suspensions.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed in any source opened; communal economic ethics point mildly toward protection of the poor but adherents are not documented as taking a side.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not stated; opposed to control by dominant groups.

party-commands-army.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: No source describes party discipline; Karenga's US Organization was disciplined but the ideology states no rule on it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Diop's federal plan requires African states to hand part of their sovereignty to a continental body so that resources and planning can be shared; this is about an African union, not the EU as such.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Asante accepts coexistence of faiths and Karenga is secular.

common-currency.rationale: Diop's federated Black Africa implies economic and monetary unification.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Diop argued that Black Africa's peoples share a common cultural heritage and language base that makes a continental federation possible, and Asante calls for continental African nationalism across existing states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: US Organization sought a separate political structure, not mere cultural autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Asante values Back-to-Africa tradition yet Afrocentrism also fights for diaspora rights; split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Afrocentrists put cultural consciousness and agency at the centre of change; Smith notes Asante faults Marx for attending to production rather than cultural norms.

ban-cartels.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not stated; inferred from minority-protection concerns.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Asante says analysis considers sex and gender, but no source states a position on quotas; adherents appear split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Diop's federated Africa; inferred for self-reliance.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

moral-incentives.rationale: Nia and Imani emphasize purpose and duty.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Karenga's US Organization trained a youth self-defense wing, but no source states a theory of armed vanguard revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Asante argues that African American students should be placed at the centre of instruction rather than at its margins and calls curricula a vital starting point.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Diop describes imperialism as first killing a people spiritually and culturally, and Ani reads colonial domination as Europe's core drive; tutelage is the premise they reject.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: Afrocentrists favour teaching centred on African heritage, not loyalty to the existing nation-state, though pan-African pride is encouraged.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: Karenga's Kawaida and Asante's emphasis on correcting Eurocentric bias suggest support for measures that aid Black people; no source addresses admissions directly.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: the sources give no position on money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: Asante argues commerce harmed Africa and the Nguzo Saba stress cooperative economics, suggesting scepticism of capitalism, though no collapse theory is stated.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: opposition to colonial legacies and support for African self-determination implies rejecting a former empire's claim to influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: Diop favoured economic and political unification of Africa, and Asante criticised the effects of international commerce, but no source calls for delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the Kawaida stress on shared Black struggle and solidarity points away from dividing workers into exploited and privileged, though no source says so.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Afrocentrism is built on resisting racial discrimination and Kawaida stresses collective rights and community.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: no source addresses constitutional design; adherents critique the US constitutional order while valuing rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Diop argued for undoing the colonial division of Africa and for continental political unification, which implies that colonial borders carry little authority.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from Afrocentric appeals to older African political forms and to self-determination; not stated directly.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the Nguzo Saba stress on collective unity (Umoja) and collective work (Ujima), which sits badly with individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the self-determination principle (Kujichagulia) and pan-African liberation politics; not addressed directly.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Genuinely indifferent: monarchy versus parliament is not an Afrocentric question, and adherents cite both older African kingdoms and modern republics.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the Kawaida and Kwanzaa emphasis on harmony with the natural world; not addressed directly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Genuinely indifferent: no source takes a position, and adherents hold varied views.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the communal values of Umoja, Ujima and Ujamaa, which stress mutual obligation within the community.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from Asante's agency theory and Karenga's Kawaida, which call for active community-building and struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Asante and Ani hold that dominant Eurocentric culture and media shape how Africans see themselves, and Ani says oppression persists because people accept Europe's definitions of reality.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Ani argues that domination works through people's agreement with European definitions of reality and weakens once that agreement is withdrawn.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Karenga condemns predatory appropriation of others' resources and Diop saw Africa's resources exploited from outside; a structural surplus-transfer theory is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from pan-African unity, which seeks a shared African citizenship over narrow national rights.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the self-determination principle and Diop's call for African federation under African direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Kujichagulia and Ujamaa stress building one's own institutions, and Diop wanted Africa to develop its own resources through federation.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from pan-African unity, which opposes new border disputes among African states.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's centring of African peoples and its claim to political agency; not stated directly for settler states.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Genuinely indifferent: anti-fascism is not a theme in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: many Afrocentric thinkers draw on Pan-Africanist socialism and would not equate the two; not addressed.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the movement's centring of the African diaspora's history, in which slavery is the defining injustice.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of Eurocentric historical narratives; monuments to condemned figures are not addressed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: Karenga's Kawaida assigns complementary gender roles and focuses on community uplift; not addressed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Kawaida's complementary gender roles; not addressed directly.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Asante rejects European frameworks as universal templates, and Diop and Asante propose an African federal state grounded in African traditions and proverbs.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the movement treats the military as outside its cultural and political programme and favours popular self-determination.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the communal values of Ujima and Ujamaa, which treat all work for the community as valuable.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the communal family values of Kwanzaa's Nguzo Saba (Umoja, Ujima) and traditional African kinship ethics; no source states it directly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; Diop's pan-African federalism and Asante's cultural focus give no position on merit examinations versus election or patronage.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the self-determination and economic-independence themes of pan-African thought and Diop's call for continental autonomy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between communal family traditionalism and liberal individual choice.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed; the communal, consensus-minded ethos hints at accountable leaders but no source mentions recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the communal and cooperative economics of Ujamaa and Ujima, which favour collective provision over private individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the Afrocentric appeal to traditional African communal land custom; not a documented plank of Asante, Karenga or Diop.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; assumed from general support for accountable, self-determined government, a weak inference.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the Afrocentric valuing of African languages and Diop's advocacy of promoting indigenous languages alongside any continental lingua franca.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial pan-African concern with African control of African land and resources; not stated in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the Afrocentric critique of structural Eurocentric bias in institutions; adherents rarely address disparate-impact doctrine by name.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Karenga contrasts social justice with gospels of personal prosperity, and Asante says Afrocentricity is more about humanity than materialism and domination.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; pan-Africanists backed African liberation movements, but Afrocentrism as a scholarly project takes no stance on arming insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on African self-determination and sovereignty, which opposes imposed intervention by a great power.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from Karenga and Asante tying economic power to political and cultural freedom and from communal Ujamaa values.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; pan-African self-determination suggests sympathy but no source states it.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; communal values and self-determination are weighed against open pan-African movement.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the cooperative economics and Ujima collective work and responsibility of the Nguzo Saba.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; cultural nationalism and civil-rights traditions are split.

non-intervention.rationale: Afrocentrists oppose outside interference in Africa, but non-intervention as a universal rule is not stated; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Academic Afrocentricity does not advance such claims, though critics link some popular strands to antisemitism; inferred and contested.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Kawaida and Kwanzaa emphasise family and community; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the stress on exposing erased history and on open knowledge.

local-production.rationale: Ujamaa cooperative economics and self-reliance (Kujichagulia) suggest local production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Karenga built the structured US Organization and Diop favoured federal unification; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; Diop favours continental federation over narrow national states.

religious-nation.rationale: Karenga is a secular humanist and Afrocentric identity is cultural and not tied to one religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on self-determination and resistance to Eurocentric hierarchy.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; Diop's pan-African federalism favours pooling at continental level, while local self-determination points the other way.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the Nguzo Saba principle of cooperative economics (ujamaa), which stresses shared ownership of enterprise.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialism and sympathy with socialist and communal models, which rarely treats communism as an enemy.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from ujamaa and communal self-reliance, which favour community-run over private provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Karenga once called Christianity a white religion and urged secular humanism, yet Imani and spirituality are core values and Ani prizes African spirituality, so adherents split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Afrocentrists stress the destruction wrought by slavery and imperialism rather than capitalism's progress; inferred, since Ujamaa still accepts profit-making businesses.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida stresses complementary gender roles while others in the movement favour equality, so adherents are split.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; communal child-rearing is valued but public services are not discussed, so inferred and split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: Kwanzaa uses Swahili, a language with Arabic loanwords, and the movement does not call for linguistic purging.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its stress on self-determination and redress of historical injustice.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ujima and Ujamaa call for collective work and community-owned businesses, and Karenga's programme names economic cooperatives as a structure of unity, though not a wholesale reorganization into small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its stress on minority self-determination and rejection of assimilation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Asante rejects the Marxist paradigm while Karenga condemns predatory individualism and offers cooperative economics, an African third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Africa is treated as the ancestral homeland of African peoples, so a historical tie to land is plausibly valued; no source states a land-claim principle, so this is inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No Afrocentric source denies the Holocaust; inferred from the scholars' engagement with genocide as historical fact.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Karenga's secular-humanist Kawaida gives no basis for criminal penalties, though cultural traditionalism splits adherents.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the emphasis on self-determination (Kujichagulia) and agency, which sits poorly with suppressing organisations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Karenga's secular humanism, which gives no role to state enforcement of religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Diop and Ani condemn colonial rule as cultural and material destruction of Africans, and Afrocentrism arose against it.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic legal doctrine outside the movement's scope; adherents have no common position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular-humanist Kawaida stance, which does not make religious law a test of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the communal principles of Umoja, Ujima and Kujichagulia, which favour collective decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Afrocentricity puts culture and race at the centre and Asante rejects class-centred Marxism, so overlapping-oppression analysis is not its framework; adherents vary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; cultural-nationalist traditionalism and academic Afrocentrism would likely split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and no clear adherent consensus.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is organised around race and culture rather than a left-right axis.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the communal and cooperative ethos of Ujima and Ujamaa, which values creative collective work.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular-humanist strand and pluralist stance, though some adherents are Muslim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida is a secular humanism, so authority is not grounded in God; inferred, not stated.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's valuing of cultural expression, including African dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the community-protective ethos of the Nguzo Saba.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the cooperative economics of Ujamaa, one of the seven principles.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the defence of self-determination and from nationalist traditions that value self-defence.

rich-first.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the communal, cooperative economics of Ujamaa and Ujima, which favour shared advance.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Diop's call for a federated, united Africa implies independence from outside powers; the statement itself is not discussed.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule sits poorly with Diop's federal, self-determining Africa and Karenga's communal values; inferred, not stated.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Nguzo Saba principle of Ujamaa promotes cooperative economics; user-owned credit is inferred from it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Pan-African self-determination and Diop's call for continental unity imply resisting outside economic dictation; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Nothing in Afrocentricity favours wealth qualifications, and its communal ethos points to broad participation; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Karenga and Asante stress African cultural agency but do not center this ecofeminist claim, and adherents are divided on gender questions.

reification.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida and Asante's link of economic to political freedom suggest sympathy with this critique of markets; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Asante ties economic freedom to cultural and political freedom, so formal rights without control of media would seem hollow; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not addressed directly; broad support for law applied equally is inferred from the movement's demand for equal standing.

racial-franchise.rationale: Afrocentrism asserts African agency but its scholarship does not call for race-limited franchise, and Karenga's secular humanism favours equal rights; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; support for broad popular participation is inferred from the movement's communal, self-determination values.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from communal accountability and the collective-responsibility principle Ujima.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida is secular-humanist and Afrocentrism has no stated rule on religious marriage; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotting by religion is foreign to its stated principles; support for black-owned business (Ujamaa) is not aimed at a religious minority.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition is outside Afrocentric writing; the communal, consensus ethos of Umoja and Ujima might favour deliberation, but nothing sourced says so, so it is left neutral.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Afrocentrists urge reclaiming African spiritual traditions and rereading imposed religions on African terms, but this is not a stated doctrine on religious law; inferred from the cultural-reclamation theme.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Asante links economic freedom to political and cultural freedom, and the communal Ujima and Ujamaa ethic suggests wariness of concentrated wealth; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Afrocentric thinkers are split, with some cultural nationalists traditionalist on sexuality and others supportive; no source states a common position.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Afrocentrism values African spiritual traditions and Karenga treats spirituality as part of culture, so state atheism promotion is unlikely; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Critique of policing is common among modern adherents, but cultural nationalism favours community self-defence and order over abolition; inferred and contested.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Diop proposed a federated Africa and Afrocentrism values group recognition, so power-sharing is plausible but not directly stated.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Nguzo Saba principles of Ujima and Ujamaa stress community-based self-help and cooperative economics, though not against government aid explicitly; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The movement does not address term limits and adherents hold no common view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; the communal emphasis suggests openness but there is no documented position.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Asante, Karenga, Diop and Ani do not take up this question; with no stated Afrocentric position, this answer is inferred from the cultural-agency focus and adherents would vary.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split between tradition-minded and egalitarian views, and Kawaida emphasises complementary gender roles in some writings; no source settles it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida has been criticised for complementary gender roles while other Afrocentric scholars favour equality; adherents are split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the communal, solidarity-based outlook and pan-African internationalism; not stated in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the communal ethos of Umoja and Ujima, which favours collective housing security; not stated in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the communal ethos of Kawaida, which values collective ownership of knowledge and works; not addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the stress on cultural self-determination and not national service; not addressed in the sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the strand's anti-colonial, pan-African self-determination; not addressed in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial self-determination, which rejects foreign military presence; not stated in the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the strand's centring of the history of slavery and colonialism; the sources do not discuss formal state recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the communal Nguzo Saba values of Ujima and Ujamaa, which favour shared work and cooperative economics.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Karenga's Black nationalism, which accepted armed self-defence; not stated in the sources.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Diop wrote that the history of Black Africa stays suspended in the air until it is connected to Egypt, and Afrocentrists trace a continuous African cultural line from Kemet to the diaspora.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the Kawaida stress on complementary roles; not addressed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from Kawaida's emphasis on shared African identity and complementary gender roles; not stated in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Kwanzaa honours ancestors and heroes as part of its cultural and spiritual framework; sacred veneration of national martyrs is inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Asante's Afrocentricity stresses spiritual and cultural values as a basis of liberation; the good-versus-evil framing is inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Afrocentrists treat Africa as the cultural and spiritual source of all African peoples, but academic Afrocentricity does not call for mass return; Asante sees diaspora Africans as agents in their own locations.

culture-before-state.rationale: Karenga's US held that a cultural revolution must come before the political one, and Kawaida treats culture as the source of a people's direction.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the strand's stress on African-centred spirituality; not stated in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The sources do not address it, and adherents may differ between womanist and complementary-role views.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the pan-African aim of African control of African economies; not addressed directly.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Diop proposed a federated Africa united by shared culture and language; applying this to regions is inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its emphasis on self-determination for African peoples.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the communal and cooperative values of Kawaida and Ujima.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the communal ethos of Umoja, Ujima and Ujamaa.

second-chamber.rationale: Afrocentrism has no stated position on legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Ujamaa, or cooperative economics, is one of the Nguzo Saba, which favours communal ownership; inferred about the exact form.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Diop's pan-African federalism and the cooperative ethos suggest confederal structures; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Kawaida stresses family as a pillar of community, so a family-supporting wage is inferred as agreeable.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by any source, and adherents have no common line.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by any source, and adherents have no common line.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not united on financial-privacy questions.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not united on online-anonymity questions.

person-over-state.rationale: The communal ethos of Umoja and Ujima puts collective well-being ahead of the individual; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Ani sees matter as a living expression of spirit and ritual as a way to realign people, and Kawaida includes spirituality and ethics as a core area of culture.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; Diop's federalism is continental, but nothing is said on regional powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's emphasis on traditional African agriculture and scepticism of Western technology.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Karenga's programme calls for local, national and international Black united fronts built on a common identity, interests and challenges as African people.

racial-pride.rationale: Asante ties an Afrocentric education to Black students' self-worth, and Karenga created Kwanzaa so Black people would celebrate themselves and their history.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-colonial and anti-imperial outlook.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Diop argued that Black Africa's peoples share a linguistic and cultural unity that grounds one nation across colonial borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from pan-African unity and the communal Nguzo Saba ethos, which favour one shared body of people over religiously separated electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from pan-Africanism's view of colonial borders as imposed by Europe to divide African peoples.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the communal ethos of Ujima and Ujamaa and the emphasis on education as liberation; not stated in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed beyond general respect for the environment; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Kuumba asks each generation to leave its community more beautiful and beneficial than it inherited it, and Karenga extends repair to the world.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Adherents are split: Kawaida stresses complementary roles for women and men, while other Afrocentric writers stress equality.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from pan-African self-determination and peace-oriented communal values; not stated in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial, self-determination stance, which opposes the secret treaties by which Africa was divided.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from Diop's call for an economically united, self-reliant Africa; the sources do not discuss capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Black nationalist currents tied to Kawaida valued community self-defence, so a state-only monopoly is unlikely; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Black nationalism and pan-Africanism criticised imperial wars; not stated for all state wars, so inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Nguzo Saba stress collective work and responsibility (Ujima) and cooperative economics (Ujamaa); inferred for unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The communal ethos of Umoja and Ujima suggests support for helping low-paid families; no source states it.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Afrocentrists tend to see austerity as hurting Black communities, so binding borrowing limits are unlikely. Inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Asante ties economic freedom to political and cultural freedom, and Diop sought African unity against colonial economic dependence.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Diop and Karenga aim to build African and Black institutions rather than a general smashing of the state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Ujamaa cooperative economics is a stated principle, so an open-ended pluralism of systems is less likely; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the communal and harmony-with-nature outlook suggests resistance to pricing nature. Inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Karenga is a secular humanist and the focus is peoplehood and culture, not a sacred nation; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; relieving debt fits the communal ethos and concern for Black economic disadvantage. Inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Black Power era cultural nationalism often described Black communities as internally colonised; not in my sources, so inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Karenga's secular humanism and Asante's agency theory assume dignity for all people; a fixed nature is not stated. Inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; a communal ethos suggests support for public media that tells Black history. Inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Kwanzaa and Kawaida draw on African spiritual traditions without a documented claim that all religions share one truth; adherents are split on religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: The communal, cooperative ethos of Ujima and Ujamaa suggests support for protecting farmers through cooperatives; inferred, not stated.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Diop's pan-African federalism sought strong continental power, but no source discusses nuclear arms, so no side is inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida is cultural nationalism and communal in outlook but the sources do not discuss a separate workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Afrocentrists criticise outside judgment of African customs, but also defend women's dignity; adherents are split and the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Kawaida's principles stress family and community and the standing of women; equal inheritance is inferred, not stated.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Diop's thesis of the genetic kinship of African languages implies treating them as one family; applied to this question it is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The communal ethos of Umoja and Ujima favours collective responsibility over private lawsuits; inferred, not stated.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Afrocentrism values traditional African institutions and cultural continuity, so a recognised role for customary leaders is inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Karenga's call to repair a degraded environment points this way, but liberty trade-offs are never discussed, so this is inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Afrocentrists criticise racial bias in the criminal justice system, which suggests opposing fixed sentences; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The sources do not address immigration or language requirements, and a pan-African outlook gives no clear side.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Communal, cooperative values suggest support for organized labor, so mandatory-membership rules are not opposed; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Pan-African and civil-rights concerns about disenfranchisement suggest opposition to stricter voter ID; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Rejection of a single dominant (colonial) religious tradition suggests equal recognition; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Diop's federalism and Kawaida stress communal, substantive self-determination over procedure alone; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Kawaida's emphasis on family and community values suggests a traditional view, though adherents vary; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Self-determination and anti-colonial emphasis suggests opposition to state censorship; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The communal ethos favors collective provision over individualized cash replacement; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Kujichagulia affirms every person's right to self-determination and freedom, and no Afrocentric source restricts women's political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Critiques focus on colonial religion, not religion as a cause of women's oppression; African spiritual traditions are valued; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Afrocentrism builds identity on African peoples and heritage, so adherents generally do not treat race as an empty construct, though Asante frames it culturally; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Communal values and state-supported development suggest support for such agencies; inferred, and not documented.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the communal, cooperative ethos of Ujima and Ujamaa in the Nguzo Saba; first-claim private ownership is never discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Afrocentrism's sources never address international criminal courts, and adherents are split between distrust of Western-dominated courts and support for accountability.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Karenga's Kawaida is described as secular humanist and no source asserts scriptural inerrancy; inferred from that.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Kawaida emphasis on community and the Asante-style stress on agency for all members; no source discusses gender in self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Not addressed by Afrocentrist sources; adherents range from Pan-African socialist to non-socialist views and none discusses bureaucratic planned states.

indirect-election.rationale: Diop's federal Africa and Kawaida's communal governance are never framed in terms of indirect election, so adherents have no clear position.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from Karenga's secular humanism and Kwanzaa's non-sectarian design; national church status is not discussed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on self-determination and cultural self-definition; no source addresses minority regions directly.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; self-determination suggests sympathy for local say, but adherents are not documented as taking a position.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Diop and Asante seek continental unity that overrides the colonial partition, though they work through federation rather than border redrawing.

simple-living.rationale: Asante sets humanity over materialism and Karenga criticizes prosperity gospels; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the stress on self-determination and protection of peoples against cultural erasure; no source addresses settlement restrictions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, communitarian stance of Kawaida; conscription is not addressed by the sources.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Afrocentrists treat Africa as the ancestral source of identity and Kawaida centres ancestral heritage, though diaspora adherents relate to it culturally rather than territorially.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: No Afrocentric source supports this; inferred from Asante's stress on personal dignity as central to law.

close-ties-china.rationale: Diop looked to China and India as development models, but Afrocentrists do not take positions on alliances; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Afrocentrists see African peoples everywhere as one people with shared interests, but state protection of co-ethnic minorities is not stated; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Karenga speaks of everyone's right to a just share of the good and goods of the world; a compensation duty for appropriating resources is inferred, not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the communitarian Nguzo Saba sit uneasily with full self-ownership, so this is inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources consulted; inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed in the sources consulted; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Karenga builds through organizations and united fronts, and Diop founded parties; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Karenga condemns predatory appropriation and gospels of prosperity; applied to business privileges this is inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Karenga's Umoja seeks unity across religions and Asante seeks to reduce religious obstacles to African integration; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Diop proposed rebuilding African culture on its ancient roots while mastering modern science and energy, and Asante's manifesto calls for an African renaissance.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from later Kawaida's commitment to the freedom of every person.

national-resource-control.rationale: Diop's federal plan rests on Africans exploiting the continent's own energy and mineral resources collectively, and Afrocentrism rejects foreign predatory appropriation.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Kawaida's communitarian, collective-work values; distribution theory is not stated.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from its communitarian economics and Pan-African outlook; the tax itself is not discussed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: It treats Eurocentric structures as a continuing source of subordination for African peoples.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the Black cultural-nationalist tradition of resisting unjust order; not stated directly.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Kwanzaa's valuing of collective work (Ujima); automation is not addressed.

multipolar-world.rationale: Diop and Asante call for a federated United States of Africa as an independent centre of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from Kawaida's communitarian economics; the labour theory is not stated.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Loyalty is to African peoples and their diaspora rather than to a national state, so the link is not assumed; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Cultural recognition and African identity are central to the movement, ahead of class-only politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred; its political programme is Pan-African and communitarian, not party-led socialism.
